A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work, Towards Efficient Contrastive PAC Learning. All pages and mathematical content support comparison. Neither version contains appendices, figures, or tables.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms, theoretical bounds, and proofs, including the multiple-negative extension, but no original empirical results.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical. Its added proof and discussion do not report experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same hinge-loss SDP relaxation, matrix constraints, and eigenvalue decomposition to recover representations. The multiple-negative objective in Section 3.3 is already present in v1; expanded explanations do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical tasks for training or evaluation. Multiple negative examples are treated theoretically in both, and noisy data remain an open question.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. Newly cited work on metric learning and contrastive optimization supplies context, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports empirical splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, preprocessing, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions lack empirical ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, and case studies. V2's discussion of noisy examples and labels proposes future research rather than reporting a robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. The probability statements in the theoretical generalization guarantees remain unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or changed. Corresponding error and sample-complexity bounds in Sections 3.1–3.3 are unchanged; the added Corollary 12 proof concerns an existing result.

T1.justification: Definition 1 changes the required output from a hypothesis in H to an arbitrary mapping from U to B, permitting improper learning. V2 also supplies the previously omitted Corollary 12 proof and makes the existing margin assumption explicit in Lemma 9. The principal theorems and numerical bounds are retained.

C1.justification: The headline contribution remains efficient contrastive PAC learning of linear representations under a margin condition. However, Definition 1 weakens the formal learning requirement by dropping membership of the returned hypothesis in H, narrowing what the PAC-learning claim requires.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds a conjecture that neural-network contrastive learning is difficult because contrastive examples already alter the linear optimization landscape. It also identifies noisy examples and labels as an unresolved extension. Existing questions about other distances and nonlinear representations remain.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, measured runtime, experimental hyperparameters, or code/data access information is introduced. The expanded SDP discussion concerns the existing mathematical construction.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens research positioning: it connects the loss to Mahalanobis metric learning [VB15], discusses stationary-point guarantees [YWQ+22], credits established SDP techniques [WS11, dGJL07], and adds literature on negative examples, halfspace learning, and robustness. These additions explain several previously undocumented relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, expands the convex-relaxation explanation, improves cross-references, and updates author contact information. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The two hinge-loss displays numbered (2.2) and (2.3) in v1 are combined into v2's (2.2), and some multiline inequalities are reset on one line. Both retain the same single-column format without figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and completeness through fuller attribution, clearer relaxation exposition, and an explicit derivation for Corollary 12. Relaxing Definition 1 better accommodates the existing relaxation-based learner, although it weakens the output-class requirement. The unchanged algorithm and bounds make the overall gain limited.
